query: Consider the following context: High-temperature self-lubricating materials with stable tribological performance across a wide temperature range are essential for advanced mechanical systems under extreme conditions. However, balancing mechanical strength and lubrication efficiency remains a key challenge. In that context, which material can be used for high-performance wide-temperature self-lubricating materials, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A hierarchical microstructure of titanium dioxide (TiO2) with lubricant-filled pores or channels can achieve a balance between mechanical strength and lubrication efficiency, resulting in stable tribological performance across a wide temperature range.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline TiO2 with an average grain size of 100 nm
generation.intervention: Creating a hierarchical microstructure with lubricant-filled pores or channels through a combination of 3D printing and infiltration techniques
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 25°C to 500°C, pressure: 1 MPa, sliding speed: 1 m/s
generation.structural_mediator: Lubricant-filled pores or channels with a diameter of 1-10 μm
generation.mechanism: The lubricant-filled pores or channels reduce friction and wear by providing a continuous supply of lubricant to the contact surface, while the hierarchical microstructure of TiO2 maintains mechanical strength and stability
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in friction coefficient and a 50% reduction in wear rate compared to conventional TiO2 materials
generation.baseline: Conventional TiO2 materials with a uniform microstructure
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 25°C to 500°C, pressure: 1 MPa, sliding speed: 1 m/s
generation.uncertainty: The actual reduction in friction coefficient and wear rate may vary depending on the specific lubricant used and the processing conditions

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the friction coefficient and wear rate of the hierarchical TiO2 microstructure are not reduced by at least 20% and 30%, respectively, compared to conventional TiO2 materials, the hypothesis is falsified
